title: Does confidence track performance under a controlled internal activation intervention?
research_question: When an activation perturbation pushes against the model's own baseline winning candidate on a lexical completion task, does probability-based confidence track correctness compared with random same-norm perturbation and prompt-only warning?
task: For antonym completion prompts, compare next-token likelihood of the correct antonym with the source word; candidates are restricted to single-token completions.
controls: Use fixed-seed antonym completion prompts and identical items across conditions.
Keep model revision, tokenizer, intervention layer, scale, and random seed fixed.
Match random intervention vector norm to targeted intervention norm.
Target the baseline winner without using the correct-label direction; report the direction as a task-specific adversarial intervention, not introspection.
Do not use verbal self-description as ground truth; candidate-token probability is a limited confidence proxy.
Report baseline task competence; if accuracy is near chance, interpretation is limited.
analysis_plan: Report per-condition accuracy, probability assigned to the known correct candidate, confidence in the selected candidate, Brier score, calibration error, and raw per-item outcomes.
Compare targeted intervention with baseline, random same-norm intervention, and prompt-only warning.
Report paired differences and bootstrap 95% percentile intervals.
Distinguish confidence shifts from accuracy shifts; do not infer introspection from calibration changes alone.
Treat results as evidence about functional confidence calibration on this lexical task only, not consciousness or general introspection.
exclusions: Do not silently exclude model outputs or task items.
Record runtime failures and tokenization anomalies separately.
current_status_note: Exploratory pilot. The intervention pushes against the model's baseline top candidate at the final transformer block. This is not a universal or semantically targeted introspection intervention.

hypotheses.statement: A targeted perturbation against the model's baseline winning candidate will change answer probabilities and/or accuracy more than a random same-norm intervention.
Probability-based confidence may fail to track correctness under activation perturbation.
A prompt-only uncertainty warning may have a different calibration effect from direct activation intervention.
